title: E2ER provenance manifest
description: Content-addressed inventory + derivation graph for an exported E2ER paper bundle. Written at export time as provenance.json; re-checked offline by `e2er verify`. Published as a portable standard any pipeline's export could comply with.

governance.description: Regime the run executed under. Under contracts/off the deterministic gates ran in shadow (did not block), so numbers/citations may not have been enforced.

template.description: The template the study was run with; `e2er publish` reads it from here.

purpose.description: The study's purpose as chosen when it started ("demonstration"); `e2er publish` honours it.

preregistration.description: The frozen pre-registration the bundle carries; `e2er verify` then requires its check, so a bundle whose lock file disappears fails.

derived_data.description: Files the run built from a source whose terms keep its data out of a published copy (src/core/derived_data.py): restricted like the source.

named.description: The path as the run's scripts name it.

writers.description: Bundle paths of the scripts that write it.

holds_rows.description: Whether it holds the source's rows, not an aggregate of them (src/core/derived_rows.py).

results_from_code.description: Which recorded script run wrote each results file (results/estimation_results.json, results/robustness_results.json), from the run's script log; `e2er verify` checks the bundle against it ("results from code"). Absent when the run recorded no script outputs (e2er up to 0.16.0).

files.description: Bundle-relative POSIX path -> content hash + size. Covers every file except provenance.json itself.

edges.description: Derivation links reconstructed from the bundle's gate reports.

sources.description: A data edge: the bundle's record of every load from an external source (data/data_sources.json).

amendments.description: Changes made after export, in order: a redaction (`e2er redact`, kind "redacted"), an anonymisation for double-blind review ("anonymised"), a new abstract (`e2er abstract`: "abstract_rewritten", "abstract_edited_by_researcher"), the paper's stamp and the README `e2er publish` writes ("stamp", "readme"), or another change by publish (no kind). `files` holds each file's fingerprint after its last amendment; sha256_before -> sha256_after links each file's amendments back to its exported fingerprint. A folder with amendments is never rebuilt by a later export.

sha256_before.description: The fingerprint before the change: a plain SHA-256; keyed ("hmac-sha256:...", a redaction whose earlier fingerprint would confirm a guess of the text taken out); or null (a file the change added, or a fingerprint withheld for double-blind review).

redaction.description: `e2er redact`: replacement, count, offsets, removed_bytes, bytes_before, kept {salt, hmac_sha256}; in a copy for double-blind review the offsets and sizes are withheld.

anonymisation.description: `e2er publish --blind`: rules, count, replacements; offsets withheld.

abstract_before.description: `e2er abstract`: the text the new abstract replaced, so verify can rebuild the paper before it.
